question: Two trains having lengths of 160 m and 140 m are running at speeds of 100 km/hr and 130 km/hr, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Same Direction) = 130 − 100 = 30 km/hr.

**Total Distance** = 160 + 140 = 300 m = 0.3 km.

**Time** = Distance ÷ Speed = 0.3 ÷ 30 = 0.01 hours.

**Time in minutes** = 0.01 × 60 = 0.6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/939be2b985ce33bd73d9660a91cbee958777f9940d0b69a2fce6729d50d49536.png] 

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 160 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 140 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 100 km/hr

Speed of second train (S₂) = 130 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = S₂ − S₁

Time = (Total Length) ÷ (Relative Speed)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance to be covered = 160 + 140 = 300 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 130 − 100 = 30 km/hr

⇒ Convert speed to m/s: 30 × (5/18) = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Time in seconds = 300 ÷ (25/3) = 300 × 3 ÷ 25

⇒ Time in seconds = 12 × 3 = 36 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 36 ÷ 60 = 0.6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 0.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). In **opposite directions**, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **seconds to minutes**, divide by 60.

Train Crossing Problems

When a train crosses another train or a platform, the **total distance** is always the sum of their individual lengths.</p
